answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying trust to a costly, verifiable work history rather than to mere identity claims. To forge standing, each agent must complete paid, audited tasks over time, so its reputation cannot be copied or instantly created. Fake accounts echo no real track record, and peers check that history before trading, like a reef that only grows slowly and cannot be faked overnight. An attacker would have to fund months of genuine work for every fake identity, making mass forgery far more expensive than the fraud it could earn.
